This exists because 'I sent this' came back as 'Beworben' (applied) in
German and 'Candidatura inviata' in Italian: five of ten locales narrowed
a button that records ANY outbound touch into one that records a job
application. The English was under-specified and the translator had no
way to know. Fixing the English fixed that one; this file is for the
cases where no English phrasing short enough for a button can carry the
Add an entry when a key's meaning depends on something not visible in the
string. Not needed for ordinary labels — this is a cost per key, so keep
it to the ones that would otherwise drift.
Keys here are NOT part of the catalogue and are never shown to a user.
The leading underscore keeps this note out of the notes themselves.
board.mark_sent: A button. Records that the user sent an outbound message of ANY kind - a first approach, a follow-up, or a posted letter. Do NOT narrow it to a job application: it is used for every rung of the follow-up sequence.
rules.unsupported: A column heading over a list of job-title words that rule a posting out. The user's own voice, addressed to the app.
rules.strong: A column heading over a list of words that guarantee a posting is read. Pairs with 'Never show me' as its opposite.
rules.contextual: A column heading. 'the title' means the job title of a posting, not the title of a document or a person's honorific.
detail.near_duplicate: Introduces another job posting that looks like the same vacancy. Followed by a job title and a company name. 'Posted' here means published as a job advert, not sent by post.
settings.key_forget: A button that deletes the stored API key from the operating system's credential manager. Not 'forget' in the sense of a person forgetting.
funnel.swept: A count of job postings fetched from the job-data provider this morning. 'Swept' as in gathered up, not as in cleaned.
funnel.gated: A count of postings excluded before any reading, because the user had already permanently rejected them.
tab.needs_review: A tab holding postings the screen killed on a term that matched INSIDE a longer job title - so the kill may be wrong and wants a human look.
board.col.role: A column heading in a job-search tracker. The JOB or POSITION being pursued at that employer (for example 'General Manager'). Not a role in a play, not a permission or access role, not a function within a team.
board.col.posted: A column heading over a DATE. The date the job advertisement was PUBLISHED by the employer. Nothing to do with posting a letter or with postal mail. If the language distinguishes 'published' from 'sent', use 'published'.
board.col.last_contact: A column heading over a DATE. When the user last sent something OUT to that employer - an email or a letter they sent themselves. It is a date, not the name of a person, and not the most recent incoming reply.
board.col.first_tracked: A column heading over a DATE. When this employer was first added to the user's tracker. Not when the job was posted, and not when the user first made contact.
board.col.url: A column heading. A web link to the original job advertisement. 'Posting' here means the advertisement, not postal mail.
board.col.location: A column heading. Where the JOB is based - a city or region. Not the user's own location and not the employer's head office.
board.col.salary: A column heading. The pay stated in the job advertisement, as free text (it may be a range, or blank when the advert says nothing).
settings.data_heading: A heading over a legal notice in an app's settings screen. 'Job postings' means advertisements for jobs. Keep it plain and factual, not marketing.
settings.data_body: A legal notice about licensed data. 'Redistribute' and 'resell' are legal terms of art - use the equivalents a licence agreement would use in this language, not casual synonyms. 'Shortlist' means the postings the user has marked to pursue. 'Competing job service' means a rival job board or job-data product.
settings.data_terms_link: Link text to a terms-and-conditions page. 'Terms' here means the legal agreement, not conditions in general and not search terms.
detail.gaps_title: Heading above a list of the requirements a job advert states. Not 'keywords' and not a score. Keep it neutral: it introduces both good and bad news.
detail.gaps_missing: Followed by a comma-separated list. 'Evidence' means the person's own CV and career factsheet, not proof in a legal sense. Do NOT translate as 'you are unqualified' — the list is informative, not a verdict.
detail.gaps_none: Reassuring but factual. Avoid congratulation; it means only that nothing STATED is unsupported.
detail.gaps_preferred: Introduces things the advert says it would LIKE, not things it requires. The distinction is the whole point — never render this as a requirement.
board.write_application: Button. Produces a tailored CV and a covering letter for this application. 'Write' as in compose a document, not as in save to disk.
board.interview_brief: Button. Produces a private briefing document for the person to read before an interview. Not a summary of the job and not something sent to anyone.
settings.report_heading: A section heading in Settings. 'What Dawnlist writes' means the text the AI generates - its verdicts on job postings and the draft messages it composes. NOT the app's own interface text, and NOT what the user writes.
settings.report_body: Explains a complaints route required by Microsoft Store policy. 'Report it' means send a complaint to the developer, NOT file a report or generate a document. 'It will be read' is a promise that a person reads it - keep that promise explicit, it is the part the policy requires.
settings.report_link: A link that opens the user's email client to complain about AI output. 'Report' is the verb TO COMPLAIN ABOUT, not to file or publish a report, and not to denounce a person. 'AI-generated content' is the text the model produced. Several languages narrow a bare 'report' to a written document - do not.
settings.subscribe_heading: A section heading in Settings, on the Mac App Store build only. 'Your subscription' is the customer's own subscription to Dawnlist, bought from Apple. Not a mailing list and not a newsletter.
settings.subscribe_body: Explains that the job feed needs a paid subscription while the rest of the app does not. 'Board', 'brief' and 'tracker' are named features of Dawnlist and already appear elsewhere in this catalogue — use the SAME words you used for them there.
settings.subscribe_button: A button that starts an Apple purchase. The verb to TAKE OUT a paid subscription. Not 'follow', not 'sign up for updates', not 'subscribe to a channel'. Apple's own App Store wording in your language is the right register.
settings.subscribe_restore: A button. Apple requires it. It recovers a subscription the person ALREADY PAID FOR on another Mac or before reinstalling — it does not refund, repeat or cancel anything. Apple's standard wording for restoring purchases in your language is what people expect here.
settings.subscribe_working: Shown while waiting for Apple. Keep it short; it sits under two buttons. The ellipsis means work in progress.
settings.subscribe_done: Shown after a successful purchase. 'The feed reads for you' means Dawnlist will search job postings on the person's behalf, starting with tomorrow's morning run.
settings.subscribe_unavailable: Shown when a purchase cannot be started at all — purchases disabled on the Mac, or the App Store not reachable. It is about the STORE being unable to take payment, not about the person being refused.
board.record_reply: A button. Records that the EMPLOYER answered - any reply from their side, not a message the user sent. It moves the opportunity to whichever stage is chosen in the dropdown beside it. Do not narrow it to 'accepted' or 'interview'.
board.record_no_offer: A button. Records that the employer said no. It closes the opportunity and every task under it. 'No offer' is the outcome the employer gave, NOT the user withdrawing or giving up.
board.confirm_title: The title of a yes/no confirmation dialog shown before either of the two buttons above writes anything. 'Outcome' here means the employer's answer.
funnel.screen_drift: A warning on the results bar. {now} and {before} are whole numbers already converted to percentages - do not add a second % sign beyond the one in the string. 'Screening rules' are the user's own keyword rules that remove postings before anything is read.
